newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares down, summertime blues set in.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares down, summertime blues set in.

text.p: Share prices and central market turnover eased Thursday on Lithuania's stock exchange and brokers said they were prepared for summer holidays further to dampen activity on the bourse.
"It is very silent, no really serious stakes of shares moved," said Kestutis Kvainauskas, a broker with Vilniaus Bank. "It means we are somewhere around the summer holidays."
"We don't expect anything special to happen on the market," said Kestutis Kupshys, a broker with Mendes Prior Europe. "Time for summer vacations, as volumes stay at a low level."
The official list fell 16.08 points to 887.16 points. Group A shares eased only 7.79 points to 1918.34 points, but Litin G slumped 64.40 points to 1682.09 points.
The losses came amid lower central market turnover, which slipped to 501,000 litas from 810,000 litas.
"We expect next week to be about the same," Kvainauskas said. "We don't expect any movements until the autumn."
"Maybe there could be a one-of-a-kind event but the general trend is still nowhere," Kupshys said.
Alytaus Textile showed the most activity on the central market, turning over 286,000 litas at 0.20 litas a share.
"It shows that the process of combining smaller stakes into larger ones is underway," Kupshys said.
Hermis Bank, which surprised brokers by edging down to 175.90 litas from 180 litas, saw low activity, turning over only 26,000 litas on the central market.
Vilniaus Banks also lost ground, trading at 224 litas from 230 litas, but turned over only 16,000 litas.
Brokers expect both to climb slightly in the near future and say Vilniaus Bank shares start looking attractive when they get down to 220 litas.
